description.text: Elastic, the Search AI Company, enables its customers to transform data into answers, actions, and outcomes with Search AI. While search technology revolutionized information retrieval through its ability to instantly return relevant results from massive datasets, it struggles when it comes to understanding context and generating insights. AI, on the other hand, excels at analyzing complex patterns and generating insights, but it lacks the ability to find and access specific information within vast data stores. The Elasticsearch Platform (“our platform”) combines the precision of search with the intelligence of AI to help our customers and community solve real-time business problems, unlock potential value, and achieve better outcomes. Our platform, available as either a cloud service or a self-managed software, allows our customers to find insights and drive AI and machine learning use cases from large amounts of data. We offer three Elasticsearch-powered solutions—Search & AI, Elastic Observability, and Elastic Security—that are built on our platform. We help organizations, their employees, and their customers find what they need faster, while keeping mission-critical applications and infrastructure running smoothly and protecting against cyber threats.

about.description_short: Elastic (NYSE: ESTC) integrates its deep expertise in search technology with artificial intelligence to help everyone transform all of their data into answers, actions, and outcomes. Elasticsearch, which is the foundation for its search, observability, and security solutions, is used by thousands of companies, including more than 75% of the Fortune 100. Learn more at elastic.co.

analysis_md:
# ESTC — Elastic N.V.
Pass-1 v5 run, 2026-10-19. Engine release 5.4.0. All figures below are copied from key_numbers.md, dcf_numbers.json, ttm.json or fundamentals.json — none are recomputed.

## What it is
The "Search AI Company": Elasticsearch and the Elastic Stack sold as one platform across enterprise search (now including vector/AI search), observability and security, subscription-led, deployed self-managed or as Elastic Cloud. Price $95.25 (nasdaq_quote_api); market cap $10.212B — in scope under $40B. Latest prints: FY26 (ended 2026-04-30) revenue up 17.26% YoY on the engine blend inputs, and Q1 FY27 (ended 2026-07-31, filed 2026-08-28) revenue $478 million, up 15% YoY, with current RPO up 21% and RPO up 27% YoY and operating cash flow of $132 million in the quarter (company release, 2026-08-27).

## Owner's earnings
Conservative definition (OCF − capex − SBC) is the binding one here, because SBC is the whole story:
- **TTM base used (ttm.py, through Q1 FY27 ended 2026-07-31):** OCF: FY $326,894,000 − prior YTD $104,835,000 + current YTD $132,004,000 = **TTM $354,063,000**. Capex: FY $5,092,000 − prior YTD $656,000 + current YTD $590,000 = **TTM $5,026,000**. SBC: FY $298,435,000 − prior YTD $69,935,000 + current YTD $74,782,000 = **TTM $303,282,000**. Shares (current-YTD weighted diluted): **104,640,231**. **TTM OE total $45,755,000 → base OE/share $0.44** (base_source: ttm_json).
- SBC of $303,282,000 against TTM OCF of $354,063,000 is why owner's earnings are a rounding error next to a $95.25 price: the cash business exists, the owners' share of it after paying staff in stock does not, yet. Q1 FY27 alone shows the same shape — GAAP operating loss of $24 million vs non-GAAP operating income of $77 million in the release, the gap being predominantly SBC.
- Latest FY (FY26): OE total $23.4M, OE/share $0.22. Normalized 3-yr median OE/share: $0.04 — see BASE_DIVERGENCE below for why the median was rejected and the TTM base used instead. OE-positive years: 3 of the last 5. One history caveat: statements.json flags a basis break in the FY21–FY22 SBC rows — the filed annual ShareBasedCompensation fact is $2,500,000 in both years, while the same filings' quarters sum to $40,078,000 (FY21) and $141,194,000 (FY22). On the quarterly sums FY22 OE would be -$138,007,000 and the 5-year positive count 2 of 5, not 3 of 5. Both years sit outside the last-3-FY window and the TTM legs, so no scored figure moves; the annual-fact extraction is an engine matter, noted here rather than silently relied on.
- Maintenance definition is not quoted as a separate total here: no computed maintenance total for the TTM period is in the outputs in front of me; the conservative series is the one the score rests on.
- Balance sheet: net debt $-197.8M (net cash), per key_numbers.md, on the TOTAL:LongTermDebt basis in dcf_numbers.json.

## Moat: 4/10 — weak-to-narrow
Justification: a real platform with developer mindshare, one-stack breadth across search/observability/security and genuine migration friction, plus ~75% gross margins — but no cycle of positive ROIC to show for it, hyperscalers forking and bundling against it, and SBC eating most of the cash it generates.
- Evidence first (fundamentals.json): gross margin ran 73.1% / 72.3% / 74.0% / 74.4% / 76.1% across FY22–FY26 and 75.5% TTM — the product carries software economics. The ROIC proxy (after-tax operating income over equity + debt − cash) ran the other way: -1.134 in FY22, -0.537 in FY23, -0.134 in FY24, -0.056 in FY25, -0.025 in FY26 — improving every year but still negative, because GAAP operating income is still negative. A moat of 7+ on that ROIC history would need a reason the history understates the franchise; the honest reason available (SBC-heavy growth spend) is itself the moat problem, since the spend is what the owners pay.
- FOR: Elasticsearch is the default search/data platform for a large developer base, embedded across search, observability and security on one stack; data integration and cluster-tuning switching friction — workloads, indexes and pipelines are costly to migrate once in production; ~75% gross margins; enterprise cohort compounding (Q1 FY27 added the most >$100K ACV customers in company history, cRPO +21%, RPO +27% YoY, AI-feature use in that cohort 37% vs 21% a year ago, per the company release).
- AGAINST: ROIC proxy negative every recent year; hyperscalers and larger rivals on every flank (AWS OpenSearch — a fork of Elastic's own platform — Splunk/Cisco, Datadog, Microsoft, Google, per the 10-K competition section); open-source roots cut both ways, with native vector databases (Pinecone, Qdrant, Weaviate) and MongoDB Atlas attacking the AI-search growth story; no proven pricing power at the GAAP line (operating margin -1.9% in FY26, -5% in Q1 FY27 despite ~75% gross margins); SBC $303,282,000 TTM with the diluted count growing 3.9%/yr.
- A 4 gives CAP = 7.2 years: growth holds 2 years, then converges linearly to the 2.5% terminal rate over 7.2 years, 15-year projection.

## DCF — final run (2026-10-19)
Growth sanity check: the engine blend is 13.76% (5-yr revenue CAGR 23.38%, 3-yr 17.61%, latest YoY 17.26%, each reduced by the -3.85pp share-count adjustment on a per-share basis). The base start of 13.8% sits below the latest revenue prints (FY26 +17.26%, Q1 FY27 +15%) for a written reason: those prints are company-level revenue growth, the model grows OE *per share*, and the 3.9%/yr share-count growth is deducted before the blend — that deduction, not assumed deceleration, is the gap. The bull start (18.8%) is roughly the current company-level print carried per-share with slower dilution; the super-bull start (25.8%) is above anything recently printed and is defensible only as a 10%-weighted tail in which AI/vector search re-accelerates the top line (Q1 FY27 sales-led subscription +18%, RPO +27% are the early shape of it) — it is not a forecast. Probabilities were shifted bear-ward from the 10/25/30/25/10 defaults to 15/30/30/15/10 per the OE_VOLATILE flag instruction. OE multipliers are the defaults 0.75/0.90/1.00/1.10/1.25. Price $95.25.

| Scenario | Prob | Growth start | OE mult | IV@15 | IRR |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Super bear | 15% | 1.8% | 0.75 | $2.61 | 2.84% |
| Bear | 30% | 8.8% | 0.90 | $4.10 | 3.07% |
| Base | 30% | 13.8% | 1.00 | $5.49 | 3.30% |
| Bull | 15% | 18.8% | 1.10 | $7.26 | 3.59% |
| Super bull | 10% | 25.8% | 1.25 | $10.63 | 4.16% |

- **Probability-weighted: IV@15% $5.42 (-94.3% vs price), IV@12% $7.31, IV@10% $9.42, weighted IRR 3.30%, base-case IRR 3.30%**
- **Tier by numbers: D**, and the band is D at both ends (bear 3.07%, bull 3.59%). Diagnostics (key_numbers.md): OE yield 0.46%, terminal value 20.1% of IV@15%, scenario spread 4.07x, net debt -4.22x normalized OE, 5.7 months since FY end.
- Method range: on the rejected normalized median base ($0.04/share) the preliminary run's weighted IV@15% was $0.54 — the TTM base is roughly eleven times kinder and the verdict does not move. Even the super-bull IV@15% ($10.63) is about a ninth of the price. This tier does not rest on the base choice.

## Flags — every fragility flag resolved
- **DILUTION** (share count growing 3.9%/yr): real and structural — TTM SBC is $303,282,000, and Q1 FY27 SBC of $74,782,000 vs the prior-year quarter's $69,935,000 (ttm.json legs) shows it still rising in dollars. It is already deducted twice in the right places: in full in the OE base, and via the -3.85pp growth adjustment. Buybacks ($380,104,000 TTM per fundamentals.json) roughly offset issuance in count terms but are a cash cost the OCF-based OE does not refund.
- **OE_VOLATILE** (OE/share spans >3x over 5 years): real — the series runs from deeply negative through $0.04 (FY25) and $0.22 (FY26) to $0.44 TTM as OCF scaled faster than SBC. Handled by the TTM base plus the bear-shifted probabilities (15/30 on bear-or-worse vs the 10/25 default).
- **NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE** (2024, 2025): in both flagged years the gap is non-cash add-backs and tax, not operations. FY25: net income -$108,114,000 vs OCF $266,168,000 — a $374,282,000 gap whose largest bridges in statements.json are the SBC add-back of $257,782,000, deferred revenue +$147,112,000 and deferred income taxes +$57,431,000, partly offset by the receivables build (-$48,903,000 — the balance grew, and statements.json carries the line at cf_sign -1) and other working-capital lines; FY25's tax line was a $76,545,000 expense, so no valuation-allowance benefit distorts that year. FY24: net income of $61,720,000 was flattered by a $184,476,000 income-tax benefit with a $186,166,000 valuation-allowance change (and FY26 net income was positive only because of a $370,067,000 benefit dominated by a $390,506,000 valuation-allowance release, FY26 10-K tax note). Net income is unusable as an earnings measure across this window; the OCF-based conservative OE used throughout is unaffected by these non-cash items.
- **SHARES_FALLBACK** (2019): the engine found no count under its diluted-share tags for 2019 and fell back to the period-end outstanding count (73,675,083) recorded in the shares_tag column. statements.json's extraction does carry a filed weighted basic-and-diluted count of 54,893,365 for FY19 (basic and diluted are equal in a loss year), on which FY19 OE/share is -$1.23 rather than the CSV's -$0.91 — the fallback flatters that one history year, and the engine's tag coverage is a code matter. Either way 2019 sits outside the last-3-FY base window and does not touch the TTM legs.
- **IRR_AT_FLOOR** (super bear): at $95.25 the super-bear IRR (2.84%) sits within 0.5pp of the 2.5% terminal growth rate, so read it as "at most ~3.0%", not a precise figure. The weighted IRR (3.30%) is not at the floor, but the message is the same: this price is beyond the model's useful range.
- **BASE_DIVERGENCE** (latest FY $0.22 vs 3-yr median $0.04): the median observation is FY25 itself ($0.0389826/share) — the negative FY24 print (-$0.90) sits in the window but is not the median. FY25's OE was only $4,041,000 because SBC of $257,782,000 consumed 96.8% of that year's $266,168,000 operating cash flow; the median is a genuine print, but it is the early point of a steep SBC-leverage ramp, not the current run-rate: SBC/OCF has since fallen to 91.3% in FY26 ($298,435,000 / $326,894,000) and 85.7% TTM ($303,282,000 / $354,063,000), and OE/share has risen every step ($0.04 → $0.22 → $0.44 TTM on a consistent ttm.py construction). The TTM base was used; the median is retained above as the method-range floor and the verdict is identical on either.
- **LOW_OE_YIELD** (0.46%): agreed, and it is the verdict — at this price essentially the entire return case is future SBC leverage that has not happened yet.
- **WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD** (4.07x): real; confidence is low, and even the top of the spread ($10.63) is nowhere near the price, so the spread does not threaten the tier.
- **BIG_NET_CASH** (net cash 4.2x normalized OE): noted — net debt is $-197.8M, so a slice of the $95.25 price is a cash pile rather than the operating business. Against a $10.212B market cap the cash does not change the arithmetic that matters.

## My thoughts / overlay
- The debate on ESTC is not growth — revenue compounding in the mid-to-high teens with RPO growing faster is fine — it is conversion. Free cash flow looks strong only because it adds SBC back; on the owner's definition, $354,063,000 of TTM operating cash flow becomes $45,755,000 after $303,282,000 of SBC and $5,026,000 of capex.
- What would change the answer is SBC dollars flattening while OCF keeps compounding: OE/share has gone $0.04 → $0.22 → $0.44, so the direction is right, but the base would need to multiply many times over — not grow by tens of percent — before a $95.25 price clears even a 10% hurdle (weighted IV@10% is $9.42).
- Risks to the short side of this verdict: an AI-search re-acceleration (the super-bull tail), a hard SBC reset under new comp discipline, or a takeout — none of which the owner's-earnings method can price, and none of which rescue the tier on filed numbers.

## Final verdict
- **Final tier: D** (weighted IRR 3.30% on the TTM base; D on the median base too, and D at both the bear and bull ends of the band)
- Confidence: **Low** (wide scenario spread, a base that depends on the TTM-vs-median choice even though the tier does not, and a super-bear IRR at the model floor)
- One-liner: Real Search AI platform, moat 4/10, but owner's earnings are a rounding error after SBC — weighted IRR 3.3% and IV@15% $5.42 vs $95.25 price; it would need to fall to about $5.42 to clear a 15% hurdle on the current TTM base.
